title: On-call & Incident Response: Runbooks, Postmortems, Game Days, and Communication Templates
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response practices, runbook templates, postmortem requirements, game day exercises, on-call rotation guidance, and customer communication templates. It is intended for on-call engineers, incident commanders (ICs), support, and engineering managers.

Scope

- Applies to all production-facing services: api-gateway, inference-runtime, routing-service, cache-layer, and metrics-collector.
- Includes detection, triage, mitigation, escalation, communication (internal and customer-facing), post-incident analysis, and continuous improvement.

Key contacts and channels

- PagerDuty policies: "Production-Api-PD", "Inference-HighPriority-PD"
- Slack channels: #oncall-internal, #incidents, #postmortems
- Incident Zoom template: zoom.us/j/INCIDENT-REDWOOD (assigned by IC)
- Status page: status.redwood.ai

Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and severity classification

SLOs (examples)
- api-gateway: P99 latency < 300ms, availability 99.95%
- inference-runtime: P95 latency < 700ms, availability 99.9%

Severity definitions (triage rules)
1) Sev 1 (P0) — Production outage or customer-impacting failures causing broad service interruption or data loss
   - Examples: inference-runtime down in a region, API 5xx rate > 25% for > 5 minutes, customer-facing SLA breach
   - Objective: mitigate within 15 minutes, restore service or enable graceful degradation
2) Sev 2 (P1) — Major degradation, significant customer impact for a subset of users
   - Examples: increased latency causing timeouts, partial downstream failures
   - Objective: mitigate within 60 minutes
3) Sev 3 (P2) — Minor degradation or elevated error rates without widespread impact
   - Objective: response within business hours; fix in next sprint if not urgent

Roles & Responsibilities

- Primary On-call Engineer (Primary): First responder for alerts from PagerDuty. Responsible for initial triage, short-term mitigation, and documenting actions in the incident channel.
- Secondary On-call (Secondary): Backup for Primary; responsible for escalation and assisting with mitigation.
- Incident Commander (IC): Assigned for Sev1/Sev2 after triage identifies broad impact. Owns the incident lifecycle (coordination, communications, decisions, runbook execution).
- Communications Lead: Coordinates internal and customer communications (may be the IC for small incidents).
- SRE Lead / Engineering Manager: Handles personnel escalations, postmortem sign-off, and follow-up remediation prioritization.

On-call rotation and expectations

Rotation model (example):
- Team: Eng-SRE on-call rotation
- Shift length: 1 week (Mon 09:00 UTC -> Mon 09:00 UTC)
- Handoff checklist (to be completed in #oncall-internal):
  1. Verify PagerDuty schedule and escalation policy
  2. Confirm access to production dashboards (Grafana), logs (Loki/ELK), and runbook links
  3. Note any ongoing incidents or maintenance windows
- Time off and swaps: Swap requests must be completed in PagerDuty and announced in #oncall-internal. Team lead approval required for extended swaps (>2 weeks).
- On-call shift compensation and expectations: follow People Ops policy in company handbook (link in Related pages).

Alerting and noise management

- Alert thresholds and run rate targets: aim for < 4 actionable alerts per on-call shift per person.
- Alert enrichment must include: service, endpoint, sampling of recent error logs, top affected customers, relevant Grafana dashboards, and suggested runbook steps.
- If noisy alerts exceed threshold, IC/Primary should create an incident to address root causes and update alerting rules.

Escalation flow (high level)

1. Primary receives alert and performs initial triage (5-15 min): verify alert, identify affected service, gather evidence (logs, traces, metrics).
2. If unresolved within 15 minutes for suspected Sev1, call Secondary and notify on-call manager.
3. For confirmed Sev1/Sev2, designate an IC and Communications Lead. Create a dedicated Slack incident channel #incident-<YYYYMMDD>-<service>.
4. IC posts incident status to #incidents and creates a status page entry (see Status page templates).
5. IC coordinates mitigation, applies runbook steps (see Runbook section) and escalates to platform or product teams as needed.
6. Once mitigated, IC moves incident to Postmortem stage and assigns owners for actions.

Runbook templates and examples

Runbooks must be short, actionable, and executable. Include: severity, preconditions, impact detection, mitigation steps, rollback steps, verification, and post-incident checks.

Example: inference-runtime-high-cpu-runbook
- Preconditions: Elevated CPU utilization on inference-runtime pods in cluster-<region> (CPU > 85% for 5+ minutes).
- Impact detection: P95 latency > 1s and increased 5xx responses. PagerDuty alert: inference-runtime-high-cpu.
- Mitigation steps:
  1. Confirm with Grafana dashboard "inference-runtime/cpu" and Kubernetes metrics.
  2. If autoscaler not scaling: check HPA status: kubectl -n inference get hpa inference-runtime
  3. If pods stuck in Pending or CrashLoopBackOff: kubectl describe pod <pod> and check events; restart if OOM or transient failure: kubectl delete pod <pod>
  4. If sustained traffic spike: enable emergency traffic-shaping: set routing-service weight to 0.5 for non-critical customers (CLI: rctl set-weight --service inference-runtime --group noncritical --weight 0.5)
  5. If mitigation requires rollback of recent deployment: follow deployment-rollback runbook (point to /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks).
- Verification:
  - P95 latency back to < 700ms and 5xx rate < 1% for 10 minutes
- Post-incident checklist:
  - Create postmortem, collect inciting change, and assign remediation actions

Standard runbook fields (table recommended in Confluence):
- Title | Owner | Service | Severity | Trigger | Mitigation commands | Verification | Rollback | Related runbooks

Postmortem process and template (required for Sev1/Sev2)

Timing:
- Postmortem draft due within 48 hours of mitigation completion
- Final postmortem reviewed and published within 7 business days

Required postmortem sections:
1. Summary: brief, non-blame description of incident and impact (what happened, who was affected, duration, customer impact).
2. Timeline: minute-by-minute timeline with actions and owners.
3. Root cause analysis: contributing factors and root cause(s).
4. Action items: clear owner, priority, and ETA.
5. Detection & response assessment: what worked, what failed, and metrics (MTTR, time-to-detect).
6. Follow-up: rollout plan for fixes, monitoring/alerting changes, and verification steps.
7. Learnings & prevention: changes to runbooks, architecture, or process.

Postmortem checklist:
- Assign author and reviewer(s).
- Attach logs, dashboards, and runbook links.
- Link to customer communications and status page entries.

Game days and exercises

Purpose: Validate runbooks, alerting, on-call readiness, and recovery runbooks under simulated load or failure modes.

Game day cadence and responsibilities:
- Frequency: Quarterly for SRE + product teams; monthly lightweight tabletop for fast-moving teams.
- Owner: Eng-SRE lead organizes schedule and scope.
- Pre-game day steps:
  1. Define clear success criteria and rollback procedures.
  2. Notify stakeholders and schedule a review session.
  3. Prepare canary or staging environment with production-like telemetry.
- Example scenarios:
  - Region failover for inference-runtime
  - Cache-layer eviction storm and recovery
  - Gradual traffic spike and autoscaling validation
- Post-exercise: publish a short report with findings and action items.

Status page and customer communication templates

Status page policy:
- All Sev1 incidents must have a public status page entry within 30 minutes of confirmation. Updates must be posted every 30-60 minutes for active incidents.
- For confidential incidents affecting a single customer or containing sensitive data, use a private status entry and coordinate with Security & Legal.

Status page template (public)
- Title: Partial outage - inference-runtime (us-west-2)
- Impact: Customers in us-west-2 may experience increased latency or request failures
- Status: Investigating / Identified / Mitigated / Resolved
- Started: 2026-02-14T09:12:00Z
- Next update: 30 minutes
- Notes: Short, factual description, mitigation steps taken, and ETA if known.

Customer email template (short & factual)
Subject: Incident notice — service disruption affecting inference in us-west-2
Hi <Customer Name>,

We are investigating a service disruption impacting inference in the us-west-2 region. Our engineers are actively working to mitigate and we will provide updates via status.redwood.ai and direct email.

What happened: Brief description of symptom and impacted customers
What we're doing: Actions being taken to mitigate
ETA: Estimated time to next update, not a promise to resolve

We apologize for the disruption and will follow up with a post-incident summary.

Sincerely,
Redwood Inference Support

Internal incident summary template (Slack pinned)
- Incident ID: INC-<YYYYMMDD>-<NN>
- Service: inference-runtime
- Severity: Sev1
- Timeline: root detection -> mitigation -> restore times
- Actions taken: bullet list of steps and commands executed
- Owners: Primary, Secondary, IC, Communications Lead

Runbook maintenance and ownership

- Every runbook must have a designated owner and a quarterly review date. Owners must update runbooks after any execution and increment the review date.
- Outdated runbooks (no updates for > 12 months) are flagged for deprecation.

Training and onboarding for on-call

- New on-call engineers must complete a 2-week onboarding checklist including runbook walkthroughs, a supervised on-call shadow shift, and at least one tabletop exercise.
- Required reading: this playbook, SLO and error budget docs, and service-specific runbooks.

Metrics and continuous improvement

- Track and publish the following per quarter: MTTR, MTTD, number of Sev1/Sev2 incidents, mean alerts per shift, and percent of postmortem actions completed on time.
- Run a quarterly review to drive alert tuning, automation opportunities, and runbook improvements.
